    The Smart Lens

    The header condenses to a 56px lens line; the rail becomes a map; nothing above the reading line moves.

    THE ASK

    We are getting close to a design that feels right on the document. The spine on the left is still cluttered and could be better utilized to navigate the ins and outs of the document. The main header contains great info but takes up most of the screen height when opened up, each section is crammed into the next and the margin seems cramped for the space needed for the functionality it contains. Have a team of UI and UX designers sit down with the Patina enginering and interiro design teams. Work with them to deisgn the document so that it contains the needed information and actions, while feeling uncluttered and peaceful. Explore animations, content that appears when it needs to and lends to space when it isnt needed in frame. Think of the document as a smart lens that is always adjusting focus on what is needed as the designers move through the document. Present your strongest proposal to achieve this in an html document accompanied with a high fidelity mockup showcasing how the team will accomplish this challenging User experience and UI requirements.

    Kody, 2026-08-28 — quoted as written. The same ask, with spelling normalised, opens source/instruments.md and every brief in this program.

    Four things fail today

    The same message names what still fails, in Kody's own order.

    • The spine — cluttered, and under-used as navigation.
    • The header — holds great information, but takes up most of the screen height when opened.
    • The sections — crammed into each other.
    • The margin — cramped for the functionality it contains.

    What this deck is

    A proposal, not a build. Ten seats read the document under scroll-state capture and code anatomy — five attention-and-access lenses, four practitioner personas walking the same sixteen tasks, one engineering-feasibility seat — and three refuters narrowed what they raised to a verified set. Two rival authors then drafted the strongest answer each could argue in isolation: proposal X, “the spine is the lens,” and proposal Y, “the paper is the lens.” Four critics scored both on design, feasibility, a practitioner's walk, and access; two judges and a merge author combined the winning organs into the one proposal this deck argues — never an either-or. That proposal became a clickable mockup, and this deck.

    Two Artifacts, one proposal

    This deck is the argument. A second Artifact is the clickable mockup it argues for — the same proposal, scroll-driven, at 1440, 1280 and 390.

    The mockup's Artifact link is not yet published as this deck was authored; it is recorded in RESUME.md once Fable publishes it. Read this deck's Walkthrough section against the mockup once both links are live.

    What kind of evidence this is

    Every seat named anywhere in this deck — the five lenses, the four personas, the engineering seat, the refuters, the critics, the judges — is a simulated seat: an agent reasoning from the running app, the code, and the plan, not a design team sitting in a room. The evidence under it is local dev on post-R126 main, against seeded documents, not production traffic. No usage data was available to this review.

    What the probe measured

    The pin at scrollY 280 is not a scroll effect — it is a state swap. 347.25px → 64.06px in one React commit; the first region head’s document-space Y jumps −283.19px inside that single 40px scroll step. Sampled every ∼17ms for 400ms: 23 of 23 samples read exactly 64.0625px — no interpolation in either direction.

    Folding a region drops keyboard focus to <body>. Unfolding is disciplined — focus lands on the region’s own heading — but folding calls no equivalent; a keyboard user who folds a region has to re-locate it from the top of the page.

    Cumulative layout shift over the scripted top→foot scroll: 0.1286 normal motion (20 entries), 0.1318 reduced motion (8 entries) — both in the “needs improvement” band, within 2.5% of each other. One shift of 0.1189 dominates both passes, arriving at ∼3.3–3.6s as the Schedule region’s “needs attention” banner resolves from a query — a data-arrival reflow, not an animation. The 283px ticket jump measured above does not register in this CLS total at all.

    F04 Ticket pin/fold is a single-frame cut with no hysteresis band F08 Folding a region drops keyboard focus to <body> F24 The dominant CLS shift is a silent late data-arrival, not motion

    THESIS

    A lens is a mechanism. Every sentence in it has a number behind it.

    The header is only true at the top of the paper, and one fact travels with her forever.

    So the header goes back to being the top of a piece of paper, and one 56px line under it carries what needs her, with its act, at every offset. The rail becomes the map: a drawn ladder of this paper’s own stops, one line per stop, printing what the paper is not saying. The lens only ever opens what is still ahead of her, so nothing above the reading line can move.

    Three sentences, three organs. None of them is a description of a feeling. The band’s height is a declared constant, not a measured one. The ladder’s extents are derived from the counts the ticket derivation already produces, never from a rendered box. And “adjusting focus” resolves to a single geometric predicate: a region’s height changes only while the entire region, and every pixel above it, is below the frame’s bottom edge.

    That predicate is what makes the whole proposal checkable rather than arguable. It is also what the mockup measures: a 30-step scripted scroll from the top of the paper to its foot, in both motion registers, reports a cumulative layout shift of 0 and zero shift entries.

    Mechanism from source/proposal.md §1 and §4; the shift measurement from mock/final/REVIEW-2.md item 8, a PerformanceObserver over #frame-1440. sim-verified

    The four lens laws, and the sentence that makes each one falsifiable

    The laws are the brief’s, in the brief’s own words, and they are not renamed here. Under each is the mechanism this proposal answers it with — the form in which a prober, or a designer with a still screenshot, can catch it failing.

    Law 1

    What is in frame is full.

    The region she is reading is at complete strength: every line, every number, every act, at the ratified R126 weight. There is no state in which the thing she is looking at is a summary of itself.

    Falsifiable as: every region intersecting the frame is full, every region she has passed stays full, never zero — and no region prints zero readable text. The brief asked for exactly one; that target is refused with the geometry, because a design where nothing above the reading line moves must hold two regions full when two touch the frame.

    F11 One screen scrolled and nothing has condensed yet F53 The fold is the only render-cost control

    Law 2

    What is out of frame yields.

    A region she is not in condenses to its head plus one status line. It keeps its place in the paper’s order — the same y-position in the scroll, the same neighbours, the same distance from the top — and it never disappears.

    Falsifiable as: yielding runs in one direction only. A body mounts when its root’s top comes within 240px of the frame’s bottom edge, off screen, always; there is no release threshold, so a region she has read is never taken back. The word scrollBy appears nowhere in the proposal.

    F04 Ticket pin/fold is a single-frame cut with no hysteresis band F87 Schedule glance drifts continuously under a moving seam

    Law 3

    The spine is the map, not a second copy of the paper.

    Something earns the left edge only if it is true across the whole document at once, or true outside this document. A running index that reprints the headings she can already see is failing that test with a straight face.

    Falsifiable as: a segment prints nothing at all while its own [data-region-head] is in frame, and un-yields the moment that head scrolls off. At most one segment is ever silent, and it is the one the reading window brackets.

    F22 The index lists regions but not their size or trouble F102 Active label pair duplicates the on-page region heading

    Law 4

    Nothing hides.

    Every condensation is reversible in one act, and its state is readable without hover — from a still screenshot, by someone who did not perform the transition. The specific failure to avoid: condensed must be distinguishable from empty on sight.

    Falsifiable as: a region with a number is quiet; a region with no number is empty; and the cause of a fold is printed in words, CLOSED BY YOU, never carried on a coloured tick. Clay measures 1.82:1 on rail stock, which contrast.test.ts:319-325 already asserts is below AA.

    F54 A folded region never shows whether she or the system closed it F89 I cannot tell a shipped fold from one I chose F108 An empty region’s index line looks identical to a live one

    What it is not

    Six things a reader arrives expecting from a proposal with the word lens in it. Each is refused rather than deferred, and the reason is a number or a mechanism, not a schedule.

    The refuses, from source/proposal.md §11
    What a reader will expectThe refusalWhy refused rather than deferred
    A rail that draws each region at its true height No proportional-extent map rail. On the specimen Pieces is 177px against Money’s 50px — 3.5:1 drawn for a true 10:1. Every segment takes a 36px floor first, and a proportionally-drawn Money rung would be a 6px press target — a 2.5.8 failure before it is a taste failure. The drawing carries order and reach; the count in the value line carries scale. The phrase true proportional extent is withdrawn rather than defended.
    The current region’s head pinned under the band No standing rule. Two stacked sticky bands are a header again, and SC2’s 52px of unspent budget would be spent on chrome rather than saved. The fact it would carry — which region she is inside — is printed exactly once per frame, on the paper, and the ladder’s window says where that is.
    A seam whose height eases as she scrolls No continuous seam, and no discrete one. The engineering seat’s three costed branches — days, week, weeks — are all declined. That seat’s own sentence is the reason: a continuous seam is not a header change, it is a navigation change. Every branch pays somewhere in scrollToRegion’s once-resolved scroll-margin-top, and every one is invisible to the suite because every seam assertion is jsdom. The variable is deleted and its replacements are declared constants.
    A narrower rail, to give the margin its room No 160px rail at ≥1440, and no 272px margin. 200 + 1040 + 232 = 1472 > 1440, so narrowing recovers 32px of measure at exactly 1440 and nothing at 1472 and above — three characters on a 15px line — and costs the rail 40px of its 168px inner measure, which is the whole value line. The margin’s answer to cramped is roughly 160px of vertical returned and 0px of width.
    Regions that condense again once she has passed them No re-quieting, and no scroll correction. Every alternative — a same-frame scrollBy(−Δ), overflow-anchor, a scroll-position correction — is a mechanism that has to be right every frame, on every fling, in a browser matrix that had no declared browserslist until Wave 0, to avoid moving a paragraph she is reading.
    New doors for the gaps the audit found No new capability: no PO-acknowledgement badge, no damage-claim door, no phase-wide install roster, no cross-document surface. The ask is to make the same information and the same acts occupy less attention. Each gap is real, several cost a practitioner a trip out of the document, and they are named so the next program can pick them up. The one thing taken from that set is the dates — a carrier window is a deadline, and deadlines are what both organs already carry.

    SPINE · the running index

    The rail is not cluttered because it holds too much. It is cluttered because it holds four tenses at once.

    Six things live in the left edge today. Two of them are about this minute, not about this paper.

    At 1440 the rail is a 200px column, 900px tall. Measured at rest on the rich project spread it carries 54.9% ink, a longest empty run of 270px, 8 interactive children and 18 distinct text labels. On a pre-work spread the same column carries 13.9% ink and a 657px empty run, because the marker row is the only thing on it.

    The diagnosis is not density. The top ~145px mixes leaving, the arc, the moment, and right-now — four tenses in one block. Below that, a running index reprints the headings the paper is already showing, and beneath that a session timer prints the largest number in the column.

    What the rail actually looks like now

    What the rail shows instead: position, extent, exception, distance.

    Position is the reading window — a --rule-mid bracket in the ladder’s gutter marking the frame’s share of the paper’s extent, travelling 1:1 with scroll. Extent is the drawn segment, above a 36px floor. Exception is the segment’s value line, in words: 36 LINES · 1 DAMAGED SEP 26. Distance is what the whole track carries — six stops in fixed height, so a stop’s position on the track says how far ahead of her it is.

    Extents are derived from the counts lib/document/ticket-derivation.ts:780-793 already produces — FF&E from line count × row height plus room count × head height, Money from its rung count, approvals from its record count. The ladder never measures a rendered body. A ResizeObserver on region roots would be measuring the thing the lens has just turned into a 112px reserve; the instrument would be erasing its own subject.

    And one segment is silent at a time. A segment prints nothing at all while its own [data-region-head] is in frame, because the paper is saying it there, at 24px Playfair, with its count line and its printed exceptions beneath. The moment the head scrolls off, the segment un-yields.

    Two numbers ship, not one, and the second is the honest one. The ink metric counts an element as ink over its whole rect if it has own text, a background or a border (research/measure-layout.mjs:245-253). The ladder’s segments are --rule-hair-bordered, so the track reads as continuous ink whatever it paints. So the probe also prints distinct text labels in the rail at 1440 at rest: today 18, after 13 — Put down, six segment lines, FILED WITH THIS JOB and its four door names, with the head’s three lines yielded while the letterhead is in frame. The rail gets fuller in claimed rows and quieter in words, and both numbers are reported.

    Where the mockup disagrees with the target, on the record. The clickable mockup measures the ladder at 40.8% merged ink at rest — 343px in 18 runs over an 840px rail — and 92.2% first-to-last-ink span. Against a ≥70% threshold, the strict reading misses by 29.2 points. The mockup’s ladder is flex: 1 1 auto rather than the proposal’s declared 443px track, and the gap is reported rather than closed. The label count is the instrument that survives that disagreement: an ink metric that counts a bordered track as continuous ink can be gamed, and a count of printed words cannot.

    The pre-work spreads, where the running index prints nothing today

    On the Aspen Loft proposal the rail carries a marker row and nothing else. That is not a styling failure. The spread renders zero [data-region-head] and zero [data-index-region] elements, confirmed by direct DOM query during shot capture — there is no region DOM for an index to attach to.

    The ladder answers it with one mechanism rather than a special case: the track’s height is fixed and the segments divide it, so a thinner spread gets bigger segments, not a shorter rail. Four stops means a floor of 4 × 36 = 144px and 299px distributed, plus the same four doors. Same geometry, the same 82.0% ink, the same 96px longest run — against today’s 13.9% and 657px.

    The regions themselves still have to exist. Wave 5 gives the four pre-work spreads real region wrappers and real heads so the ladder has something to index, and it is priced at weeks, not smuggled into a smaller wave.

    F12 On a proposal the rail is almost entirely empty F16 Pre-work spreads have no region DOM to index at all F20 A proposal prints eight rows of nothing above its answer F157 Pre-work rail shows no timer card at all, unlike the rich doc

    At 1180–1439 the rail prints words, and the paper loses nothing

    The rail widens from 56px to 136px and prints every label as a word. The engineering seat priced widening at weeks because it moves the paper’s x-origin. At this tier the arithmetic says it does not: page.tsx:1764 gives min-[1180px]:grid-cols-[56px_minmax(0,1fr)] and <main> is max-w-[1040px] justify-self-center. At the tier’s floor, 1180 − 136 = 1044 ≥ 1040, so the paper is already at its cap and the measure is unchanged at every width from 1180 to 1439. 140px is the exact break-even; 136 leaves 4px of slack.

    Inside px-3 that is a 112px measure: Put down prints its word at about 62px, the head prints Vandersteen and wraps PROCUREMENT / & ORDERS / 4 OF 6 at spaces and never mid-word, every segment prints the same one register and the same value wrapped to two lines, and every door prints its word.     HEADER · the letterhead and the lens line

    The header holds the right information. It also holds a whole frame of it.

    At 1440 at rest, the stack above the first region head measures 1005.31px in a 900px frame — 111.7%.

    Nothing in that stack is wrong. The letterhead names the household, the ticket derives eight true rows, the needs-attention block is the one colour-coded signal on the first screen and a junior’s eye correctly snaps to it. The defect is arithmetic: they are all printed at once, above everything, and then most of them leave.

    One full letterhead-scroll later, header and summary content still claims 60.7% of the frame and the active region gets 10.4%. Scroll a little further and the ticket pins and folds in a single frame — a 283.19px swap that never registers as a layout shift because it happens inside a sticky box.

    So the answer is not to compress the header. It is to let the letterhead be the top of a piece of paper — arrival, once, then gone — and put one 56px line under it that carries what needs her, with its act, at every offset.

    Today

    Proposed

    A letterhead, and one line.

    The letterhead keeps its arrival mark, its 40px Playfair title and its household chip. It sheds the empty vitals fields and PHASES ▸, which opens and reveals nothing; the in-hand room row moves to the rail’s doors, where the release is reachable at every offset rather than at the top alone; and pb-5 becomes pb-4 above a doc-rule-mid. It costs 148px against today’s 189.31, it happens once, and it leaves.

    Then the lens line: 56px, declared, at every width and every offset, sticky top-0 z-[4], carrying #doc-ticket-sentinel immediately above it — the only sticky element on the paper. Its lower edge is a --rule-mid 1.5px inside its own box, never a shadow, because the shadow budget is spent. Its background is --doc-paper #FCFAF6, fully opaque, so nothing scrolls through it and the composite contrast is the declared contrast.

    SC1 = 298px at 1440 at rest on the measured seed spread — 33.1% of the frame, against 1005.31 and 111.7%. Recovery 707.31px. On the Vandersteen specimen the vitals row carries real values and prints 21px, so SC1 = 319px, 35.4%. Both are stated: the specimen is the world the design must survive and the seed is the world the JSON measured.

    The number is better than either parent proposal’s because their moves are additive rather than alternative. One removed the ticket, the instruments and the letterhead’s surplus and then reserved 136px on the paper for a needs band. The other kept the letterhead whole and replaced the needs block with a 56px band. Taking both, the 152.75px needs block becomes 56px of band that is also the seam, and no reserved block stands on the paper at all.

    Where the 56 comes from

    h-14, border-box: 8.8 padding + line 1 at 11px × 1.4 = 15.4 + 2 + line 2 at 15px × 1.3 = 19.5 + 8.8 padding + --rule-mid 1.5 = 56.0. Both lines are single lines by construction — white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis — so no string it can be handed changes its box.

    What the line prints at its shortest

    At rest, with the letterhead 60px above it, line 1 prints $17,500 OUT and nothing else. The letterhead is already printing the household at 40px Playfair, the stage as the arc, and the date in its vitals, so each of those yields. Money has no yield partner — the letterhead prints no money — so money keeps its printing.

    Line 2, in every state, prints the worst standing exception with its act, and · +3 MORE when it withheld any, in --color-terracotta-ink #9C5340 at 5.41:1 on paper. When nothing stands it prints the guide sentence, Name the phases for this project with OPEN THE SCHEDULE, in charcoal. So the shortest the line ever prints is eleven characters of money and one sentence with a verb on it.

    Below the sentinel, line 1 fills out: VANDERSTEEN RESIDENCE · PROCUREMENT & ORDERS 4 OF 6, with INSTALL SEP 15 · $17,500 OUT right-flush — 50 characters left, 28 right, about 555px of 11px mono in a 944px measure. While Money is the reading stop the right-flush figure drops, because the money region’s own head is printing it. And in every state, never the current stop’s name: the paper’s own <h2> and the rail’s window both carry that word already.

    At 390 the measure is 390 − 56 = 334px, so line 1 carries the two facts the letterhead does not print — $17,500 OUT · INSTALL SEP 15, 28 characters, about 200px — and the household goes to the mobile bar’s left zone, which prints it at every offset for free. The band is 56px there too.

    Truncation is the height contract

    Line 2 at 15px in a 944px measure holds about 110 characters; the specimen’s worst standing exception is 96 before its act. When it overruns, the act’s words truncate first (SEND A REMINDER → REMIND), then the subject’s qualifiers, and never the number, the day-count, or the room.

    Because the line cannot wrap, that order is the whole of the height contract. It also retires the alternative that was on the table: a pre-ship gate reading if that cannot bring it inside one line at 1280, the band does not ship. A gate is a decision; a truncation order is a mechanism, and a mechanism is what a prober can check on a live string.

    +3 MORE is a scored act, not a count. It opens a DocSheet listing every standing exception with its own act — which is strictly more than today, where deriveTicketSeam’s .slice(0, 2) at ticket-derivation.ts:855 drops the third whole and leaves no trace of it.

The proposal does not reduce it to zero writers — it deletes the name from the tree, and replaces it with two declared constants: --doc-band-height: 56px and --doc-landing-clear: calc(var(--doc-band-height) + 1rem) = 72px. A name that no longer exists cannot acquire a second writer.

    BODY · sections, spacing and the margin

    The sections are crammed into each other because there are three answers to one question.

    Measured button-to-button at every width and every scroll state, the gaps between region heads are {6, 29, 56} px.

    Three spacings, on a list that reads as one uniform stack of seams. Header-stack-end to Schedule is 56px; Schedule to Pieces is 29px; Pieces to money-head is 6px. They are scroll-invariant and width-invariant, so this is not a responsive artefact — it is three call sites each deciding for itself.

    The sharpest case is in the tree. Approvals open is mt-6 … py-6 at project-approval-document.tsx:588; approvals folded is a bare <div data-index-region="approvals"> with no wrapper at all at :565. So folding a region silently changes the gap around it as well as its height.

    One token replaces all three. --doc-region-gap: 24px, owned by the region wrapper rather than the call site, identical whether the region is full, quiet or folded. That last clause is the load-bearing one: it is what makes a fold a change in density and not a change in the paper’s geometry.

    The lens at the middle of the paper

    FF&E at full, its neighbours yielded to their condensed line. Exactly one region carries the whole ledger; every other stop on the paper still holds its place, its head, its count and its one act.

    Folded by choice, condensed by position — told apart in a still

    Today four fold verbs print on one screen and none of them says why. A region folded by a derived default and a region folded by her look and read identically, and a designer returning to a document she folded three weeks ago — the key patina:doc-fold:{docId}:{region} outlives the session — reads the seam as there is nothing here.

    The proposal separates the two by giving each its own rule weight, its own typography and its own printed cause. A quiet region keeps its --rule-strong double rule and its 24px Playfair head, and prints a count line and one act. A folded region drops to a single --rule-mid, prints its name in italic with a mono summary, offers UNFOLD ↓, and prints CLOSED BY YOU. An empty region keeps the strong rule and the Playfair head and prints Nothing yet with no count at all.

    Which makes the discipline a single sentence: a region with a number is quiet, a region with no number is empty — and a designer reads the difference off a PNG, without hover, without having performed the transition.

    The mark that makes the distinction honest is upstream of the drawing. The latched derived default stops producing folds and becomes the region’s initial density instead, after which a FoldSeam can only ever mean you folded this. That has a visible consequence on the first screen of every project document, and it is named rather than shipped quietly: Client approvals and Schedule dates are both folded by a derived default today, and they open on arrival.

    Cause printed in words, never on a coloured tick: clay measures 1.82:1 on rail stock, which contrast.test.ts:319-325 asserts is below AA, and the offender scan at :334-338 would not catch it because it greps only for text-[var(${pigment})]. code-read

    MOTION · eleven mechanics, and their still forms

    Eleven mechanics. Every one has a form a designer sees with motion turned off.

    A reduced-motion cell that reads “n/a” is a row that was never designed. None of these do.

    Four of the eleven have no transit to reduce at all — two commit off screen, one is a render hint that changes no measured height, and one is an arithmetic gate. Four sit beside a reduce block that already ships in app/globals.css. One needs no new rule because its still form is declared inside the no-preference gate rather than outside it. One new block covers the three crossfades. And exactly one row cannot be covered by a CSS media query, which is stated as an amendment rather than dressed as compliance.

    The ambient budget stays at one: doc-breath, 3s, on the active StrataMark, in the rail, at its shipped site. No second ambient move is named. The reading window is position-linked rather than time-linked, and therefore not ambient.

    And there are zero hover-only affordances. Every state below is a printed mark or a focus state. The shipped tree has none today; this proposal adds none.

    The one declared amendment

    L-2 is the single row a CSS media query cannot cover. Its rAF handler reads matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') in JS and steps the bracket instead of sliding it. hooks/useReducedMotion.ts exists and no file under components/document imports it; the Document’s policy is nine @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) blocks plus one no-preference gate. This proposal keeps that policy except for this one handler, and calls it an amendment rather than compliance. That sentence is what makes the rest of the table trustworthy.

    The same eleven rows, drawn

    Where the hysteresis is, and where there is deliberately none

    Two systems get confused with each other, so they are separated here by their numbers.

    The mount threshold has no pair. A region’s body mounts when its root’s top comes within 240px of the frame’s bottom edge — off screen, always — and it never unmounts for the life of the document view. There is no release threshold, so there is no hysteresis pair to tune and nothing for a prober to oscillate on. 240px is defended against the specimen rather than against a sentence: one FF&E line is a 48px catalog crop plus py-2 plus a rule, 65px, so 240px is more than three lines and a three-line nudge cannot re-cross it. It is the same number at 1440, 1280 and 390, because a line is the same height at every width.

    The reading-stop resolver is where the asymmetry lives. In the clickable mockup it is two IntersectionObserver bands rooted at the frame, plus a synchronous arithmetic resolver over the same two bands: PROMOTE = [0.08, 0.38], a narrow band 8% to 38% down the frame, and HOLD = [0.00, 0.88], a wide one. A region is promoted by entering the narrow band and can only fall once it has left the much wider one — that gap is the hysteresis. Measured over a 20-step slow scroll at --motion-scale: 4, every region changes data-density at most once per step, and the sequence is monotone.

    Two more numbers govern tempo. The settle is 120ms below 40px per frame; it gates every density change and every announcement. The 700ms jump lock is the shipped one, and it gains one job: for its 700ms it forces the target stop to be the reading stop. Returning to a stop already announced within 2s is silent, so a slow re-read across one boundary does not fire repeatedly.

    Threshold, settle and jump lock from source/proposal.md §3 and §4; the two observer bands and the 20-step measurement from mock/final/FINAL.md §1(b). sim-verified

    Zero layout shift, by mechanism

    Six clauses, in the order they close the hole.

    • a. The band’s box in flow is 56px before the pin and 56px after, so the pin displaces nothing.
    • b. Its height is declared and both lines cannot wrap, so nothing it says can change its size.
    • c. A region’s height changes only while the entire region, and every pixel above it, is below the frame’s bottom edge.
    • d. A region she has passed never changes height again this session.
    • e. --doc-seam-height does not exist, so the value four consumers read cannot change mid-scroll. The schedule’s zero-height glance at schedule-rule.tsx:548 is left at h-0 and given a constant top — giving it a reserved height would create the shift it was removing.
    • f. The band’s own content is what the late-arriving red-letter query resolves into, and the band is 56px before that query returns — so the 0.1189 shift, 92% of the page’s cumulative layout shift in both motion registers, has nowhere to land.

    What that measures as. A PerformanceObserver({type:'layout-shift'}) over a 30-step scripted scroll from the top of the paper to its foot on #frame-1440 reports CLS = 0 with 0 shift entries in the normal register, and CLS = 0 with 0 shift entries in the reduced register. The paper’s extent grows from 4381px to 5106px across the same sweep, which is the design: it only ever grows below her.

    The word scrollBy appears nowhere in the proposal, and there is no scroll correction of any kind.

    From mock/final/REVIEW-2.md item 8 and R-16. sim-verified

    The reduced register, at the condensed state

    A still picture cannot show an absent transition, so this frame is drawn pixel-identical to the animated one by design. That is the claim: with motion reduced, every mark in the lens is present, at full ink, in place. L-1’s reduced form is the sentence printed instantly in place — same words, same terracotta, no crossfade.

    There is no in-product motion toggle, and the position is stated rather than left unraised. 2.3.3 is AAA and the stated bar is AA; the OS query is the control, which is what the tree does today. The opening of a region ahead is essential to the mechanic, because both the first-head recovery and the render-cost control depend on it. The dev-bar toggle is a QA instrument, not a product control.

    MOBILE

    Below 1440 the rail runs out of room to say things in words.

    At 1280 the running index survives as a 56px glyph column. At 390 it is not on the canvas at all — it is a sheet, opened from the bar.

    At 1280 the six-segment ladder still reports every register, but the column is 56px wide, so it prints glyphs, not the words a 1440 spread shows. `doc-spine.tsx`'s own comment calls the fixed 200px column's remaining measure “room to spare” for the seven-mark arc — true for the arc, not for a stage name. A 20-character stage name at 11px mono has nowhere to land, so it wraps, and the wrap lands mid-word.

    1. S2

      She keeps reading and reaches Pieces. The frame budget moves from today's 13.9 / 0 / 86.1 / 0 (chrome / header / work / other) to a target of 12.9 / 0 / 87.1 / 0 — the 64px seam becomes a 56px band and the difference goes to the region itself.

      She scrolls to the end. The band is still there, still 56px, line 2 still naming the worst standing exception — the state machine's reading state runs unbroken from the seam to the last stop. The paper carries a 520px foot margin (460 at 1280, 560 at 390) so that pressing the rail's last stop lands its head at exactly 72px, the same landing every other stop gets, instead of stopping short because the document ran out of paper first. Today's frame at the foot is 13.9 / 0 / 50.9 / 35.2; the target is 12.9 / 0 / ≥62 / ≤25.1, because the two stops at the foot become indexed regions in their own right.

    BUILD · six waves

    Each wave is worth shipping on its own. The bands are the engineering seat’s: days is one to three, week about one, weeks two or more.

Across Waves 1, 2 and 4 it switches which children the rail mounts, which grid template page.tsx:1764 renders, whether the ladder or the shipped list fills the shelved slot at doc-spine.tsx:141, and whether the density observer attaches. It does not gate Wave 3: a deleted component is not flaggable, and this path does not pretend otherwise.

    FF&E landing floorapp/globals.css:1037The same constant. The max(…, 4rem) arm goes, because 72 is more than 64 — so FF&E keeps more air than today, not less.
    Money inline clearancecommercial/money-region.tsx:48The local SEAM_CLEARANCE constant reads --doc-landing-clear. Declared locally, so a fix applied only in CSS would leave this one wrong.
    New — every focusable in the paperapp/globals.cssRegion roots were never the only landing targets. Every anchor, button, input, select, textarea and [tabindex] in the paper takes the same clearance, plus scroll-padding-bottom: 60px on the root.
    The var(…, 0px) fallback armsall four sitesGone with the variable. Nothing is registered and nothing needs to be: a declared constant has no fallback case.

    code-read Confirmed by grep over apps/designer-portal/src: app/globals.css:1026, :1034, :1037 and components/document/commercial/money-region.tsx:48, and no others.

    The regex, and the two gates that stay green

    The regex. lib/document/__tests__/stage2-approval-cutover-contract.test.ts:19 reads /data-active-section[\s\S]{0,1500}?<SectionStageLineMount/ over the raw source text of page.tsx, via fs.readFileSync. Its unit is source characters, not DOM, so a provider, a wrapper, a <Suspense> boundary, two more drag handlers or one more comment turns it red with no rendered difference at all.

    Wave 0 deletes it. The replacement — render the page, assert the mount follows [data-active-section] in DOM order — goes into app/(document)/doc/[id]/page.test.tsx, which already carries the harness. The source file stays a readFileSync contract and keeps its four other assertions at :15-17, :21-23, :24 and :25-27. code-read apps/designer-portal/src/lib/document/__tests__/stage2-approval-cutover-contract.test.ts:19

    lib/document/__tests__/shadow-gate.test.ts stays green. No depth of any kind is declared, and no fourth wearer of .doc-elevated. The band’s separation from the paper is a rule weight and the stock value step, which is what NG2 leaves available. The caveat: the gate is a readFileSync plus a regex by construction, and NG2 asks for a computed-style sweep. Green here is a source fact, not the sweep.

    lib/document/__tests__/contrast.test.ts stays green. No clay text is added to the rail, and the muted ramp’s lightest step already computes to 6.5:1 on paper, so a quiet region needs no new grey. What it does need is Wave 0’s glob: today it scans five hard-coded filenames, and a rename drops a file from the scan with no failure — a green test that has stopped testing.

    Three risks, and what proves each real in the first week of building

    The path names six. These are the three whose falsifying observation falls inside the build. The other three — the rail is still the cluttered thing; one line at rest is less than the block it replaces; the document grows under her scrollbar — can only be settled by working in it.

    Risk · where it lands · what falsifies it
    RiskWhere it lands, and its bandThe falsifying observation
    R2 — the band’s one line is not enough for a real exception new lens-band.tsx, fallback upstream in lib/document/ticket-derivation.ts. Wave 3, week. Line 2 holds about 110 characters; the specimen’s worst is 96 before its act. The height contract rests on the truncation rule. Render the specimen’s two red-letter rows and the longest live seam exception into the band at 1440, 1280 and 390, and read them. If truncation under the stated order — act’s words first, then qualifiers, never the number, day-count or room — leaves a sentence she cannot act on at 390’s 334px measure, the ranking drops the qualifier upstream before the band ships.
    R4 — one frame of lookahead is the wrong distance on a fling new hooks/use-lens-density.ts and ffe-section.tsx, 1,549 lines, unvirtualized. Wave 4, week. The seat’s own Rank 2, and the one it says the synthetic seed — three FF&E lines, no rooms — can never show. Seed a 60-line, 4-room schedule with catalog crops, open it at 1440, fling top to foot, and record blank paper where a region should be for more than one frame. A fling suppresses the settle by design, so the opens fire together at the landing; if the landing still shows an unmounted body, the lookahead has to grow — and a larger lookahead means the lens is doing less.
    R6 — two new index keys break a throw that exists to protect the index lib/document/document-index.ts:100, roots in care-band.tsx and previous-work.tsx. Wave 2. The type widening alone is days in the seat’s bands; the wave carrying it is a week, each root being emitted at exactly one mount site. Pressing Closing the book throws in the console on the first branch build — or the ladder’s bottom two segments never highlight, because the MutationObserver attach never sees a root. That second failure presents not as an error but as a rail going quiet at the foot, the thing the wave was built to fix.

    ROADS

    Seven proposals were argued, and seven were killed — each by a number, not a preference.

    Every road below was a real design in this program, drawn and defended by a seat that believed in it. Each carries the one sentence that ended it, quoted, and who wrote that sentence.

    Six of the seven were killed by an arithmetic fact: a floor, a distance, a measure, a wrap, a frame. The seventh was killed by a person weighing a working instrument against a principle — the harder kind of evidence, and the kind this program exists to produce.

    • 01

      The map rail drawn at true proportional extent

      The ladder as a scaled elevation of the paper itself — each segment drawn at its region's real share of the document's height, so the drawing itself answers extent, distance and position without a number or a legend. It was the most direct answer to F22 The index lists regions but not their size or trouble, and the most beautiful mark either author drew.

      The one thing a map is for — how much of this paper is my schedule — is the thing the drawing flattens.

      C-practitioner critique seat, Dp-11 · simulated seat

      Every stop needs a press target; the floor the target sets eats the proportion — on a 443px track, six floors spend 216px before a single pixel is drawn by extent, and an 11:1 truth draws as 3.5:1.

    • 02

      No lens line at all

      Nothing on the paper pinned. The header stayed a letterhead that leaves, the instrument moved entirely to the margin, and below the fold the paper was only paper. Removing the sticky surface entirely also removed the surface F04 Ticket pin/fold is a single-frame cut with no hysteresis band, F34 Continuous seam height breaks every region landing, F87 Schedule glance drifts continuously under a moving seam and F120 Only region roots clear the pinned seam, not their child controls land on.

      The needs band is non-sticky, so SEND A REMINDER for the six-day overdue approval is ~2,000px above her at s2. The exception's word survives on the ladder; its act does not.

      J1 judge seat, Dj1-06 · simulated seat

    • 03

      The value-free rail — six equal rungs, position and nothing else

      The rail stops carrying figures at all — no counts, no dollars, no exception marks, position only — on the principle that a rail which prints no figure cannot print a false one. The diagnosis was exact: F108 An empty region's index line looks identical to a live one, F29 Approvals emptiness printed twice on one screen and F10 Five money statements, four numbers, one screen are all the same fallback-wearing-a-live-figure's-clothes error, and this road cannot commit it.

      Y deletes it on a principle — that a rail which prints no figure cannot print a false one — which is a good principle bought with her working instrument.

      J1 judge seat, §6 “Who is worse off” · simulated seat

    • 04

      The 40px transfer — a 160px rail funding a 272px margin

      Narrow the rail by 40px and give the width to the margin, so the paper column keeps its measure and the organ Kody calls cramped for its work gets 40px wider. It was the only move in the program that answered the width half of that complaint at all, rather than answering it with vertical space and hoping nobody noticed.

      32px of measure recovered at exactly 1440 and none at 1472 and above, against 40px of the rail's 168px inner measure, which is the whole of the value line.

      J2 judge seat, merge instruction “Sections and margin” · simulated seat

      Forty pixels off the rail also carried F17 The margin never changes as I move down the paper's value line, which is the whole payload the road was trying to protect.

    • 05

      The text-free 1280 tier

      At 1180–1439 the rail would print no words at all — a hairline, a tick per stop, a clay mark for the stop she is in, every tick a press target that opens the sheet with the full names. It was the cheapest correct answer to F07 Stage word breaks mid-syllable in the glyph rail, and it introduced no new iconography.

      A hairline with six ticks is the one place in either proposal where the document stops looking like paper furniture and starts looking like a scrollbar, and it is a tier Kody works at.

      J2 judge seat, axis 6 · simulated seat

      The fight was never necessary: 1180 − 136 = 1044, which is still ≥ 1040 — the words fit at that tier without moving the paper's x-origin by a single pixel.

    • 06

      The measured band — one writer, a ResizeObserver, kept to the letter

      The band keeps its published height's name and its single writer, but a ResizeObserver measures the real box on mount and on every resize rather than only while pinned-and-unfolded — declared is the minimum, measured is the truth. It directly answered F44 Seam height is content-dependent, not a constant, where the published height already depends on which exception string is showing.

      Y's own R2 concedes a live exception string can overrun 56px; the mitigation is a pre-ship gate … which is a decision, not a mechanism.

      J2 judge seat, Dj2-13 · simulated seat

    • 07

      Releasing a region above the reading line, with a same-frame scroll correction

      Density running both ways: a region whose bottom has passed above the frame releases and a same-frame scroll correction takes back the exact height it gave up, so nothing on screen moves. It was the only mechanism that made the lens symmetrical, and it answered the render cost named in F53 The fold is the only render-cost control; FF&E is unvirtualized for a region on either side of the reading line, not just below it.

      A region that releases above the reading line takes its height with it and nothing gives it back… every pixel below it — the line she is reading — rises by 1,728px.

      C-feasibility critique seat, DC-01 · simulated seat

      The correction has to be right every frame; a trackpad fling crossing three releases in 200ms can land the correction one frame late, and no instrument in the tree records it when it does.

    Two moves this program did not re-open, because a reader will ask: NG1, one document at a time — no split view, no tabs, no persistent global nav over an open document; and NG3, the Thumb Index, removed by Kody and not re-proposable.

    LIMITS

    This deck does not claim user research, measured outcomes, or a built product.

    • No user research was run — no designer was observed, interviewed or surveyed.
    • Every seat in the panel is a simulated seat.
    • The evidence is local dev seed data — the rich document carries 3 FF&E lines and 0 rooms, so any finding that depends on a long schedule is thinner here than it would be on a real sixty-line one.
    • The mockup is a stylesheet and a script over the invented Vandersteen specimen, not the product.
    • The frame-budget figures in the proposal are design targets, not measured outcomes.
    • Nothing here is built, and no product code was changed.
